orchestration_finalization.initial_error: The shell wrapper was edited while Bash was still reading it. Both completed measurement receipts and API/dependency statistics had already been written, but final summary generation encountered a shell parse error.
orchestration_finalization.recovery: The EXIT trap removed all owned containers and their anonymous volumes. Receipt ownership was restored to workspace UID 1004, and summarize.py was executed locally against the unchanged completed measurement receipts.
orchestration_finalization.current_runner_checks: bash -n passed; the wrapper now runs the API process with the workspace UID and records the executable checksum/build info before measurement.
orchestration_finalization.dependency_oom_or_restart_claim: Not asserted: final dependency inspect was skipped by the wrapper parse error. API exit/OOM states are independently captured in each api-container JSON. Dependency memory statistics were captured after each workload.

reproducibility_limit: The initial run did not capture an executable checksum before its temporary binary was removed. Tool and dependency versions are recorded, and each plan/latency/memory receipt is retained. The current wrapper captures the checksum/build info for subsequent runs; no checksum of the completed run is invented.
cleanup_verified: A subsequent docker ps -a filtered by the tool's exclusive quickquiz.runtime-benchmark=synthetic label returned no containers.
acceptance_limits: The host is shared, with 12 logical CPUs and about 15.4 GiB RAM; all three benchmark workloads were pinned to the same two CPUs and given aggregate 2 GiB container memory limits.
The test excludes Manager, ads, SPAs, reverse proxy, production log I/O, AI, and ingress transit; load generation and validation share the API process.
The fixture administrator performs count/parity verification before the startup timer; startup measures runtime stores plus readyz with healthy seeded dependencies, not complete executable boot.
No dedicated production-node approval or one-million-question capacity claim is made.
